Checkout puts contact, delivery and payment on one page, with the order summary beside it on wide screens and folded above it on phones. Each step opens in place and turns into a short summary row when it’s done, so a finished checkout reads like a receipt: “Contact maya@example.com”, “Ship to 12 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94110”, “Method Standard · Arrives Oct 26 – 28 · Free”. Pass Stripe’s PaymentElement as paymentElement so card details go straight to Stripe and never touch your server. onPlaceOrder calls elements.submit(), then a server action reprices the cart, returns a changed result if the total moved, or creates a PaymentIntent with the attempt’s idempotency key. confirmPayment handles 3-D Secure, and onCheckStatus asks the server about attempts that never answered.

Pass the cart and three callbacks: onGetRates(address), onEstimateTax(address) and onPlaceOrder(draft, payment). Rates and taxes load as soon as the address is complete, with a short pause while someone is typing, and the previous request is aborted through its signal when the address changes. The page also handles the slow and strange cases. Pay can’t run twice, and the Change buttons lock while an order is placing. If onPlaceOrder doesn’t answer within 20 seconds, the page says it’s checking the status and polls onCheckStatus with the same idempotency key instead of offering to pay again. An item that sells out mid-checkout is taken out of the total and flagged until the shopper removes it or continues without it, and pressing Pay with gaps lists every problem in one linked summary.

describeChange
describeChange(change, { locale }) returns a sentence such as “Only 2 Stoneware cup left, so we changed your quantity from 4 to 2.”

onPlaceOrder gets a draft with the email, lines, addresses, chosen rate and the exact total the shopper saw, plus the payment request with a fresh idempotency key. Return succeeded with the order, declined with a code, requires_action for 3-D Secure, or changed when the server’s prices differ. A changed result never charges: the summary updates, a notice lists each change in plain words (“Ring vase is now $74, was $68.”) with the old total struck through, and the shopper presses Pay again at the new amount.
useCheckout
useCheckout(options) takes the same data and callbacks as Checkout and returns the state and actions it renders from.
